sources.title: Warren et al. (2010) — The genome of a songbird
sources.version: Nature 464(7289):757–762; published 2010-04-01; author manuscript in PMC
sources.locator: Abstract; Genome assembly; Gene expression and evolution; chromosome comparison; song-responsive expression results.
sources.scope: Primary structural, functional, and comparative analysis based on one male zebra-finch draft genome, forebrain samples at 50 and 850 days post-hatch, and comparison with chicken.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike; license statement appears in the article, but the version number is not stated there.
sources.rightsEvidenceLocator: Article end matter states distribution under the Creative Commons Attribution-Non-Commercial-Share Alike licence; no numbered version is given.
sources.attribution: Warren WC, Clayton DF, Ellegren H, et al. (2010). The genome of a songbird. Nature 464(7289):757–762. https://doi.org/10.1038/nature08819. Claims are paraphrased; no article text or media is redistributed.

claims.text: The study assembled a draft genome from one male zebra finch; of about 1.2 Gb, approximately 1.0 Gb was assigned to 33 chromosomes and three linkage groups.
claims.scope: A single male reference individual and the 2010 draft assembly.

claims.text: Forebrain expression data were sampled at 50 days post-hatch during the juvenile song-learning period and at 850 days in adults.
claims.scope: Two age points only; not a complete developmental series.

claims.text: Comparison with chicken found overall conservation of synteny and karyotype alongside many intrachromosomal rearrangements.
claims.scope: Two-lineage genomic comparison; not a complete account of variation across Aves.

gaps: No new multi-source species dossier is added; the existing bounded dossier covers only genome evidence.
The study does not establish geographic variation, a current reference assembly, or a comprehensive natural-history account.
